title: Grateful Dead Live at Starlight Theater on 1982-08-03
source: SBD -> Cassette Master -> PCM -> Dat -> CD

ai_review.summary: Miller’s crisp soundboard captures a scorching 8/3/82 Starlight show – Mississippi Half‑Step, Franklin’s Tower and Jerry’s soaring solos make it a standout.
ai_review.review: The recording is a clean Miller SBD that, after a quick EQ/pitch tweak, delivers clear instrument separation and plenty of punch. The performance is a high‑energy “Jerry night” with smoking Mississippi Half‑Step into Franklin’s Tower, superb To Lay Me Down, Althea, Peggy‑O, Cumberland Blues, Big Railroad Blues, The Other One and a powerful Stella Blue. While a few reviewers note minor slip‑ups (Althea a bit sluggish, Cassidy rough) the overall consensus is that this concert ranks among the best of the 1982 summer tour.

ai_rating.rationale: Over 30 reviews overwhelmingly praise the musical performance (many 4‑5 stars) and note a generally good soundboard recording despite minor pitch/bass issues, leading to a high combined rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp and clear overall; Miller’s mix is praised for instrument separation. Some reviewers mention low‑bass presence, occasional speed/pitch drift that benefits from a –1‑2% correction and modest EQ tweaks.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Strong opening set that builds momentum into an even hotter second set; the transition from Half‑Step to Franklin’s is highlighted, and the jammed second‑set sequence (The Other One → Stella Blue) keeps the energy soaring.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Repeatedly praised for tight, soaring solos, great tone, and a “ripping” performance especially on Half‑Step, Franklin’s and The Other One.
band_member_comments.Phil: Noted for solid bass work and “bombs” during jams; one reviewer called his playing lackluster on Cumberland but most praise his sync with Jerry.
band_member_comments.Bob: Complimented for slide guitar break in Minglewood Blues and overall rhythm support.
band_member_comments.Keys: Brent (keyboards) highlighted for strong contributions, especially in The Other One and Shakedown‑type jams; several reviewers call the keyboard work “great”.
band_member_comments.Drums: Generally described as tight and driving; no specific criticisms noted.
